newsitem.title: HAITI: New Dominican ambassador welcomed in Haiti.
newsitem.headline: New Dominican ambassador welcomed in Haiti.

text.p: The Dominican Republic's new ambassador to neighbouring Haiti presented his credentials Wednesday to President Rene Preval, sealing a reconciliation between the two countries after a migration crisis earlier this year.
Ambassador Rafael Julian said he hoped to strengthen economic and cultural ties between the two nations, which share the Caribbean island of Hispaniola.
"There are many important issues that we need to look at together," said Julian. "They include ecology, economics and cultural relations."

Earlier this year, mass deportations of Haitians from the Dominican Republic triggered a diplomatic crisis. Thousands of Haitians, some legally living in the neighbouring country, were snatched off Dominican streets and dumped at the border. Ambassadors from both countries were called home for consultations.
Preval met Dominican President Leonel Fernandez in February and hammered out an agreement that slowed the deportations to a trickle.

The Spanish-speaking Dominican Republic had not had an ambassador in French-speaking Haiti since the border crisis, though it never formally withdrew Julian's predecessor Eladio Knnipping. Julian said Knnipping had been in Panama since April 10.
